newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes firmer, wet Tapis premium hits 95 cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes firmer, wet Tapis premium hits 95 cts.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were mostly firmer on Thursday, supported by an overnight rally on futures markets.

Traders said some late Dubai wet cargos were traded late Wednesday, ridding the market of an October overhang. Oman barrels were still hanging over the October market as traders move their focus to November trading.
Two October Dubai cargos were sold by a trader to a U.S. major at a discount to dated Brent of under $2.00 per barrel.
The premium for October Tapis rose to quotes plus 95 cents as a producer sold 300-350,000 barrels to a Japanese refiner.

The previous deal was done between 80 and 90 cents premium. The producer said it was riasing to $1.00 its asking price with around 700,000 barrels left for October, although half a cargo could move into the Malacca refinery.
October paper Tapis rose to $22.15/$22.40 from a day-earlier $21.75/$21.95, while the November Brent/Dubai widened slightly to $2.12/$2.15 from $1.95/$2.05, reflecting the futures strength.
A trader was putting together 1.7 million barrels of October Duri crude. It acquired the barrels in lots of one million and 700,000 from two Pertamina affiliates at ICP plus 25 cents.
The move reflected the potential to arbitrage barrles into the U.S. given the firm WTI price.
A French major started selling some of its November lifting equity crude from the Gulf.
A cargo of Murban was sold to a U.S. major at ADNOC plus 19.5 cents and a cargo of Qatar Marine to another U.S. major at QGPC quotes plus 16 cents, traders said.
The second major bought a top up 150,000 barrels cargo of Qatar Marine from a U.S. major.
